newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-SECOND '97 INT'L BOND IN SEPT OR OCT.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-SECOND '97 INT'L BOND IN SEPT OR OCT.

text.p: Lithuania will likely tap the international capital markets with a second 1997 bond issue in September or October, Finance Finister Algirdas Shemeta told Reuters in an interview.
"We will have a second issue in September or October...we have some preliminary thoughts on it," Shemeta said.

Lithuania has already announced its intention to issue a $200 million eurobond this year which will be led by JP Morgan Securities. That bond will probably be launched in late spring or early summer, after the country acquires a credit rating from Standard and Poor's.
"It is too early to disclose the amount of the second bond," Shemeta said.
"It depends on the market conditions and rating, which we hope will be investment grade," he said.
"It is too early to discolse the amount, but it could be higher than our first this year," he added.
He also said that the ministry was mulling the idea of a yankee instead of a eurobond.
